governing_intent: Implement the Python invocation runtime for real CLI workers under explicit grants and fail-closed budgets, enforcing candidate custody so VERIFY requires an exact published revision independently read back from a fresh checkout.
summary: PY-06 is a bounded, coherent vertical slice. Its custody, workspace, provider, capability, budget, cancellation, retry, and verifier-independence rules are constrained by approved authority. PY-04 and PY-05 are sequencing dependencies, not unresolved owner decisions.
implementation_unknowns: Select eligible existing CLI provider adapter(s) through bounded capability probes.
Define typed port records, rejection shapes, process supervision, Git mechanics, and grant representations within the approved architecture.
Choose deterministic local Git fixtures, including an independently reachable remote, for publication and fresh-checkout proof.
Determine the minimum-cost real provider invocation that evidences the adapter path.
verification_assessment: Verification is real executable proof: actual Git worktrees, publication and fresh-checkout read-back; independent producer/verifier invocations; negative custody and self-approval cases; real child-process timeout and cancellation; one bounded real provider CLI invocation; deterministic fakes only for remaining cases; retained evidence plus Node-suite and fitness results.
material_risks: A configured CLI provider may be unavailable or unable to enforce a hard-required budget dimension; it must be ineligible rather than downgraded.
Publication/read-back must use an independently reachable repository path, not a mutable branch name or producer workspace.
Cancellation cleanup requires proven ownership and quiescence; ambiguous process identity remains an unresolved recovery condition.
Integration must preserve PY-02 custody admission and PY-04 loop semantics without treating worker success as a verdict.
Provider diagnostics, grants, and retained evidence require redaction to meet the no-secret criterion.
next_action: After PY-04 and PY-05 are accepted, release PY-06 for implementation and begin with executable negative custody, cancellation, and provider-eligibility tests.
rationale: SF-REQ-003/007/009, FD-03, SWF-09, the approved Wave 1 DAG, and the Architecture Authority fix the relevant product and architecture decisions. Remaining choices are normal category-B implementation design inside those constraints; the contract contains no independent decision center requiring a split.

provider_evidence.note: reassessment at PY-05-landed baseline, after SWF-23 repair-cycle contract section
